L-background-obligation-default-on.name: New obligation or notification enabled by default for existing callers
L-background-obligation-default-on.mechanism: A finalize step, a new notification type or a new background check becomes active by default for every caller or existing user: a pending obligation (an expected upload, an acknowledgement) that a timer later escalates, or a new event that a stored wildcard preference or master switch opts everyone into. Callers that never intended to take part create stalled records, false alarms and auto-filed tickets, or existing users start receiving messages they never asked for. Opt-out defaults hide it until the timer fires or the deploy reaches production.
trigger_signals: a finalize, close or submit step that creates a pending record a sweeper later escalates or notifies on
a boolean like *_expected / *_required defaulting to true, or inferred from weak signals
a new notification or event type evaluated against stored wildcard or master-switch preferences ({*: true})
preventive_checks: Make the obligation opt-in by the caller that will fulfil it; default off
Test that the plain path (no opt-in) creates nothing pending and never escalates; a late fulfilment may reopen it
Test an existing user's stored preferences (wildcards, master switch) against the new event and assert the documented default wins

L-nonprod-env-acts-on-shared-prod-data.name: Non-production deploy acts on production data through a shared store
L-nonprod-env-acts-on-shared-prod-data.mechanism: Staging and production share one database, queue or outbox, so any worker, sweep or drain deployed to staging runs against production rows and posts to production integrations (chat, email, webhooks). A new sweep designed as if it runs only at the production deploy releases an accumulated backlog, such as weeks-old messages, to real users the moment staging deploys. Tests run on an isolated DB, so the cross-environment reach shows up only in review or in production.
trigger_signals: a new worker, sweep, drain or reconcile job over a table, queue or outbox that more than one environment reads
the first run of a new sweep over rows that accumulated before it existed
an environment whose settings point at another environment's database, broker or integration credentials
preventive_checks: Before shipping a worker, list every environment that runs it against the same store and every external endpoint it posts to; gate its side effects to the environment that owns the rows (an environment flag or an owner column)
Bound the first run: dry-run count the rows it would act on, skip items older than a cutoff, and release any backlog deliberately

L-waiting-state-without-deadline.name: Waiting state with no deadline when its resolver disappears
L-waiting-state-without-deadline.mechanism: A record or process enters a waiting state (pending, updating, held, mismatch) whose only exit is an event from another actor: a watcher, a callback, a renderer or a follow-up flow. When that actor dies, restarts or is never started, nothing moves the state on and it holds forever: a node stops sending heartbeats, a run never settles, a badge says updating indefinitely. Tests always drive the resolver, so the never-resolves path is first exercised live.
trigger_signals: a new pending, held or verifying state that is cleared only by another process, callback or user action
a hold that suppresses a liveness signal (heartbeat, lease renewal) until a check passes
a watcher or supervisor process that may be absent after a restart or an upgrade
preventive_checks: For every waiting state write down the event that ends it and a deadline that moves it to a reported terminal state (failed, rolled back)
Test the resolver never arriving: kill the watcher or drop the callback, advance the clock past the deadline, and assert the state ends and liveness resumes

L-admission-on-lagging-load-signal.name: Admission gate decides on a load sample that lags admitted work
L-admission-on-lagging-load-signal.mechanism: A gate admits heavy jobs (parallel agent lanes, test runs, builds) when one instantaneous sample of CPU idle or load looks healthy. Jobs admitted moments earlier have not ramped up yet, so the sample still reads idle and several jobs pass together; when they ramp at once the host thrashes (load far above the core count, agents stall). Background OS work such as file indexing of new checkouts adds to it. Each admission looked correct when it was made.
trigger_signals: an admission or throttle gate that checks current CPU idle, load average or free memory once before starting each job
jobs that take minutes to reach peak usage (dependency install, server boot, test-suite ramp)
several queued jobs waiting on the same gate
preventive_checks: Count admitted-but-ramping jobs against the budget (a fixed reservation per admission for its ramp window) instead of trusting the live sample alone
Admit one job at a time with a cooldown about as long as a job's ramp, decide on a sampled window rather than one reading, and keep a hard cap on concurrent heavy jobs
